o1.biggest_strength: It correctly makes sleep, evening posting, and narrator clips the core of the plan, with strong use of the customer’s exact bedtime language.
o1.biggest_mistake: The review timing is a little muddled, saying later reviewed posts can only go live from Tuesday 24 November while the plan still uses Monday 23 November as part of the rhythm.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a full 24-post calendar or clearer week-by-week variations, and tighten the review flags so the schedule and approval dates match exactly.

o2.biggest_strength: It turns the data into a concrete 24-post rhythm with owners, deadlines, draft copy, stop-list, and a useful high/low success forecast.
o2.biggest_mistake: A couple of details are off or loose, especially the Tuesday 24 November review note and the imprecise “sleep posts nearly triple” line.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Polish a few lines to feel more unmistakably Headspace, remove the small number/timing slips, and flag review risk post by post.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 2 is a little more operational: it gives the owner the 24-post map, first production moves, and decision rules without needing much extra planning. Output 1 is slightly warmer in places, but less complete as a four-week calendar.
